summary: hex returns uppercase hexadecimal text for the bytes of a blob.
documentation: hex returns uppercase hexadecimal text for the bytes of a blob. For non-blob arguments SQLite first treats the value as text, so the hex of an integer describes its decimal text bytes rather than its binary integer representation.
returns: id and hex_text, ordered by id.
caution: Hexadecimal encoding is reversible representation, not encryption. NULL produces an empty string in SQLite; this exercise uses only blobs and NULL.
scenarios: Display binary import payloads safely in a debugging table.
Compare byte sequences in a file-format audit.
Render a short binary identifier as printable text in an export preview.
title: Render payload bytes
problem: Return id and hex(data) AS hex_text from payloads, ordered by id. Use uppercase hex with two digits per byte. Empty blobs and NULL both yield an empty string.
hint: Apply hex directly to the blob, without casting it to a number.
goal: Use hex() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
